definition: A mode of inference in which a model repeatedly feeds its own intermediate conclusions back as new input, refining them over several passes until it converges on an answer.
details: Instead of committing to a single forward pass, a recurrently reasoning model revisits its thoughts: it drafts, inspects, and revises. Modern reasoning models approximate this with long chains of thought and test-time compute, spending extra tokens to reconsider earlier steps. Quiet-STaR showed that models can learn to think before speaking by generating and reflecting on rationales token by token — a form of recurrent, self-guided reasoning.
story: Imagine a mathematician who writes every step on paper, reads it back, crosses out a bad line, and starts that line over. Boil it down and it is this: A mode of inference in which a model repeatedly feeds its own intermediate conclusions back as new input, refining them over several passes until it converges on an answer. Here is why it matters: Instead of committing to a single forward pass, a recurrently reasoning model revisits its thoughts: it drafts, inspects, and revises. More time spent reconsidering can be worth more than a bigger model. That loop of draft, check, and revise is Recurrent Reasoning.

citation.title: Quiet-STaR: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Think Before Speaking
